description: Cleanup sampling temperature. PINS: the temperature both platforms put into the OpenAI-compatible chat/completions request body -- Rust OpenAiCompatibleCleanup::DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE (src-tauri/src/llm/mod.rs) and Kotlin KlarvoApi.CLEANUP_TEMPERATURE (the value written as the 'temperature' field in cleanupText's request body). DOES NOT PIN: AnthropicCleanup's own DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE (a separate provider with a different request format; the Rust side asserts separately that it currently agrees, which is a coincidence-check, not a contract), llm/local.rs's llama-path constant (target-gated to Windows, unreachable from a Linux test run), the Whisper STT temperature (fixed at 0.0 on both platforms; the dead advanced.sttTemperature config key was removed in story 7-9), or that either platform actually sends the field on the wire (no network call is made).

Cleanup response token cap. PINS: the max_tokens both platforms put into the OpenAI-compatible chat/completions request body -- Rust OpenAiCompatibleCleanup::DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS and Kotlin KlarvoApi.CLEANUP_MAX_TOKENS. A drift here truncates long dictations on one platform only, which is silent and user-visible only as a cut-off sentence. DOES NOT PIN: AnthropicCleanup's pair, the llama path in llm/local.rs, any user-facing override (the dead advanced.llmMaxTokens config key was removed in story 7-9; this value is not configurable), or any server-side cap.

The size at or above which cleanup switches from one call to parallel chunked calls. PINS: the effective decision BOUNDARY on BOTH sides, not merely a declared number -- Rust CHUNK_THRESHOLD (llm/mod.rs, used as 'raw_text.len() < CHUNK_THRESHOLD' in chunked_cleanup) and Kotlin KlarvoApi.shouldChunk (the public seam extracted in story 7-1, 'bytes >= CHUNK_THRESHOLD'). Both are measured in UTF-8 BYTES, not characters. Each side runs its own 399/400-byte probe through production -- Kotlin through shouldChunk, Rust through chunked_cleanup (single-call path vs joined chunked path) -- rather than only reading the constant, so a flipped comparison operator is caught on both halves. DOES NOT PIN: how the text is split once the threshold is crossed (see TWIN-CHUNK-TARGET-SIZE-001), the parallelism, or any user-facing override (the dead advanced.chunkThreshold config key was removed in story 7-9; this boundary is not configurable).

Target chunk size in UTF-8 bytes, used as the fallback split offset when no sentence boundary is found in the search window. PINS: the fallback split point of Rust split_into_chunks and Kotlin KlarvoApi.splitIntoChunks, probed with a boundary-free input (a long run of a single ASCII letter) so best_split/bestSplit stays null and the split lands exactly on start + CHUNK_TARGET_SIZE on both sides. DOES NOT PIN: the sentence-boundary search window (start + TARGET/2 .. start + TARGET + 200), the punctuation set, the UTF-8 continuation-byte backoff, or the trivial-fragment merge -- those are covered by chunking-cleanup-vectors.json, not here.

The separator used to re-join parallel chunk results into the final cleaned text. PINS: a SINGLE LF (U+000A, char code 10) between adjacent chunk results on both platforms -- Rust chunked_cleanup's combined_text.push(char 10) loop (driven here through the existing MockCleanupProvider, so the assertion binds to the real join path rather than to a re-implementation) and Kotlin KlarvoApi.joinChunkResults (the public seam from story 7-1). Expressed as a char code rather than a literal so the fixture cannot be misread as CRLF or as a double newline. DOES NOT PIN: the empty-result skip rule (Rust skips the separator while combined_text is empty; Kotlin's seam has the matching isNotEmpty guard -- each side asserts that rule with its own leading-empty case -- Kotlin joinChunkResults(listOf("", "beta")), Rust a mock that blanks the first chunk by content -- but the fixture value itself states only the separator), trailing-newline handling, or the order in which chunks complete.

Default cleanup model ID for DeepSeek, and the empty-override rule that selects it. PINS: the model both platforms send when advanced.llmModelDeepseek is unset -- Rust DeepSeekCleanup::DEFAULT_MODEL (src-tauri/src/llm/mod.rs) and Kotlin KlarvoApi.DEFAULT_MODEL_DEEPSEEK. Also pins the shared empty predicate (story 7-9, Q5): the override is TRIMMED first, so a whitespace-only value counts as empty and falls back to this default -- Rust llm::effective_cleanup_model, Kotlin KlarvoApi.effectiveCleanupModel. Each side reads its own production symbol and compares it to the fixture literal below, never to the other platform's symbol. DOES NOT PIN: that a NON-empty override reaches the request (each platform asserts override flow-through in its own unit tests -- Rust pipeline::tests::spec_model_override_flows_through_*, Kotlin LlmFallbackProviderTest), the DeepSeek endpoint (TWIN-* not needed; see LlmFallbackProviderTest's URL tests), OpenRouter's model (a separate provider whose 'deepseek/deepseek-chat' literal stays hard-coded -- no override key exists, story 7-9 Q8), or any network call.

Default cleanup model ID for OpenAI. PINS: the model both platforms send when advanced.llmModelOpenai is unset -- Rust OpenAiCleanup::DEFAULT_MODEL and Kotlin KlarvoApi.DEFAULT_MODEL_OPENAI -- plus the same trim-then-empty rule as TWIN-CLEANUP-MODEL-DEEPSEEK-001. OpenAI is a candidate on BOTH the primary-selection path and the Epic-12 fallback ladder on both platforms, so a drift here is silently asymmetric. DOES NOT PIN: override flow-through (per-platform unit tests), the OpenAI endpoint, or any network call.

Default cleanup LLM model ID for Groq. PINS: the model both platforms send when advanced.llmModelGroq is unset -- Rust GroqCleanup::DEFAULT_MODEL and Kotlin KlarvoApi.DEFAULT_MODEL_GROQ -- plus the same trim-then-empty rule as TWIN-CLEANUP-MODEL-DEEPSEEK-001. This is Groq's CLEANUP model, unrelated to Groq STT ('large-v3-turbo'). DOES NOT PIN: override flow-through (per-platform unit tests), Groq's exclusion from both fallback ladders (story 12-1 AC2, asserted separately on both platforms -- Groq is primary-only), the Groq endpoint, or any network call.

Default cleanup model ID for Anthropic -- DESKTOP-ONLY, deliberately NOT a twin. PINS: the Rust side only -- AnthropicCleanup::DEFAULT_MODEL against the fixture literal below, plus the same trim-then-empty rule as TWIN-CLEANUP-MODEL-DEEPSEEK-001 via llm::effective_cleanup_model('anthropic', ..). The kotlin_symbol field is deliberately null and the Android column is a WRITTEN RECORD, not an assertion: Android has no Anthropic cleanup provider at all (drift row H5, accepted as a pure feature-port asymmetry under ADR-0016 Amendment 1), so advanced.llmModelAnthropic is Desktop-only (story 7-9, Q6). No Kotlin test asserts this entry -- TwinConstantsVectorsTest skips it by id. Same precedent as the M12 dictionary fixture. DOES NOT PIN: anything on Android, override flow-through (Rust unit tests), the Anthropic endpoint or request format (Anthropic is not OpenAI-compatible), Anthropic's absence from the Rust fallback ladder (it is primary-only, asserted separately), or any network call.

The sanitisation both platforms apply to a raw advanced.llmModel* override before it becomes the model field of a cleanup request. PINS: the shared predicate -- trim the ends, then DROP every character below U+0020 (C0 control characters), and only then apply 'empty means the provider default'. The 'cases' table below is a list of raw -> expected pairs which each half feeds through its OWN production seam (Rust llm::effective_cleanup_model, Kotlin KlarvoApi.effectiveCleanupModel); an EMPTY expected value means 'the provider's built-in default is selected'. Note the ordering the table forces: a value that is non-empty after trimming but empty after stripping (the lone U+0001 case) must still fall back to the default, so a strip-before-empty-check implementation is required. Added by story 7-9 review round 1, decision D2: the override is unvalidated free text, so a stray newline in a model ID must not forge a line in Klarvo.log or travel to the provider. DOES NOT PIN: WHICH default an empty result selects (that is TWIN-CLEANUP-MODEL-DEEPSEEK/OPENAI/GROQ/ANTHROPIC-001), the Desktop-only model-not-found warning text (pipeline::degrade_warn_msg_for_model -- Android has no equivalent), any length cap or character allowlist (deliberately none: a provider may introduce any ID shape, and D2 chose no UI validation), or any network call.
